title: The coherent Poincare transform of the structure sheaf
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety] of dimension $g\geq0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $A^\vee$ be the dual abelian variety and $\mathcal P_A$ the universal Poincare invertible module on $A\times_k A^\vee$, normalized on both identity axes, as in [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus]. Write $p_2:A\times_k A^\vee\to A^\vee$ for the second projection and $e:\operatorname{Spec}k\to A^\vee$ for the identity. Regard $e_*k$ as the coherent module supported on the reduced identity point, with structure-sheaf action through evaluation at $e$. Use derived categories of Zariski module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary derived direct image [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image]; shifts have $H^i(C[r])=H^{i+r}(C)$. There is an isomorphism
$$Rp_{2*}\mathcal P_A\simeq e_*k[-g]\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal O_{A^\vee}).$$
No restriction on the characteristic of $k$ is imposed.

source.place: Mumford, Abelian Varieties, Chapter III §13, proof of the dual-variety theorem pp.126–129 and Corollary 1 p.129 (Koszul calculation); used again in §16 pp.151–152. Primary book scan read online at https://djvu.online/file/2tC7xp3dbqGCh; local book WANTED. The statement is the derived form of that calculation, not the Riemann–Roch theorem of §16.

proof.text: Put $B=A^\vee$ and $C=Rp_{2*}\mathcal P_A$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus], $B$ is an abelian variety of dimension $g$. The projection $p_2$ is proper by [lem-kun-proper-stability], which also gives properness of the composite $A\times B\to B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The schemes $B$ and $A\times B$ are proper over $k$, hence Noetherian, and $\mathcal P_A$ is coherent, by [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent]. Moreover $p_2$ is flat: on affine product charts its ring map is $D\to E\otimes_kD$, whose target is a free $D$-module after choosing a $k$-basis of $E$. The line module $\mathcal P_A$ is locally the structure sheaf, so it too is flat over $B$ and has relative Tor dimension zero. Thus [lem-pc-bounded-coherent-finite-tor-proper-pushforward-perfect] makes $C$ perfect. By [lem-pc-relatively-flat-canonical-module-base-change], its derived pullback by every $T\to B$ is the derived direct image of the ordinary restricted Poincare module; this includes residue fields, localizations and nonflat infinitesimal quotients.

source.place: III §13 pp.126–127, base-change complex; Stacks 08EV (perfect-lemma-perfect-direct-image) and 0A1D (perfect-lemma-base-change-tensor).

proof.text: For a closed point $b\ne e$ of $B$, the normalized fibre $\mathcal P_b$ is algebraically trivial and nontrivial, by the representing property in [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], these closed points are $k$-points, since $B$ is of finite type over algebraically closed $k$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-picard-zero-cohomology] and the base change in step 1, the derived fibre of $C$ at $b$ is zero. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-finite-free-residue-model-existence] at $b$: all its ranks are zero, so $C$ vanishes on a neighbourhood of $b$. Each cohomology sheaf of the perfect complex $C$ is coherent. Its support is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed], and the density of closed points [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] applied on $B\setminus\{e\}$ shows that this support is contained in $\{e\}$. Thus $C$ is zero away from the identity.

source.place: II §8 (vii), pp.76–77; III §13 p.127, punctual support. Stacks 0BCD (more-algebra-lemma-lift-perfect-from-residue-field).

proof.text: At $e$, step 1 identifies the derived fibre with $R\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)$. By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization] and [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety] its degree-zero cohomology is $k$. Cohomology is finite dimensional by [lem-fin-proper-coherent-finite-dimensional] and zero above $g$ by [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension]; there is no negative cohomology. By [lem-sc-perfect-finite-free-residue-model-existence] choose a finite free model on an affine neighbourhood of $e$ with ranks equal to these fibre dimensions. Pass to $R=\mathcal O_{B,e}$ and denote the resulting complex by $K$. It represents the local restriction of $C$, has terms only in $[0,g]$ and $K^0=R$. Its differentials reduce to zero modulo $\mathfrak m$: each term modulo $\mathfrak m$ already has the dimension of its cohomology, so both adjacent differential ranks must be zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] and [lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension], $R$ is regular local of dimension $g$, with residue field $k$.

source.place: III §13 pp.127–129, the finite free complex at the identity; Stacks 0BCD. No coherent exterior-algebra theorem is needed.

proof.text: Let $D=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(K,R[0])$, with the usual cochain signs, so $D$ has terms in $[-g,0]$. For every prime of $R$ other than $\mathfrak m$, $K$ localizes to an acyclic bounded finite free complex, by step 2. Such a complex is split exact: starting at its last nonzero term, split the surjection onto that free term and repeat on its projective kernel. Its dual is therefore acyclic too. Consequently all cohomology of $D$ is supported at $\mathfrak m$. The complex $D[-g]$ has terms in $[0,g]$, so [lem-sfb-regular-local-punctual-acyclicity] gives $H^j(D)=0$ for $j<0$; its positive cohomology is zero by its shape. Thus $D$ is a finite free resolution of $M=H^0(D)=\operatorname{coker}(D^{-1}\to D^0)$. Since $D^0=R$ and the matrix entries lie in $\mathfrak m$, write $M=R/I$ for an ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$.

source.place: III §13 pp.127–128, reversed dual complex and cyclic cokernel; Stacks 00N0 (algebra-lemma-acyclic).

proof.text: The nonzero cyclic module $R/I$ has support only at $\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-support-power-ideal-kills] on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the coherent sheaf associated to $R/I$ and the ideal $\mathfrak m$. We obtain $\mathfrak m^N\subseteq I$ for some $N\geq1$. Set $T=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ and let $j:T\to B$ be the local morphism. The maximal ideal of $R/I$ is nilpotent, and its residue field is $k$. No assertion that $T$ is reduced is being made.

source.place: III §13 p.128, the infinitesimal cyclic quotient. Stacks coherent-support power-annihilation criterion.

proof.text:
For any $R$-algebra $Q$, finite freeness gives the natural identity
$$H^0(K\otimes_RQ)=\ker(K^0\otimes_RQ\to K^1\otimes_RQ)=\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,Q).$$
Indeed the right side is exactly the kernel obtained by applying $\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,Q)$ to $D^{-1}\to D^0\to R/I\to0$; $K$ has no negative term. The affine derived-category equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] and the base-change comparison [lem-pc-relatively-flat-canonical-module-base-change] identify the left side, for $Q=R/I$, with $H^0(A\times_kT,\mathcal P_T)$. The identity of $R/I$ therefore gives a section $s$. Its reduction at the closed point of $T$ is nonzero: under the same kernel identity it is the nonzero quotient $R/I\to k$, represented by $1\in K^0\otimes_Rk=k$. Hence $s$ reduces to a nonzero constant section of $\mathcal O_A$.

source.place: III §13 p.128, the quotient module and evaluation section; Stacks 0A1D (perfect-lemma-base-change-tensor).

proof.text: The section $s$ trivializes $\mathcal P_T$. To check this, trivialize the line module locally on $A\times T$ and write $s$ as a scalar $u$. Its reduction modulo the nilpotent ideal $\mathfrak m(R/I)$ is a unit, since the reduced section on $A$ is a nonzero constant. A lift of its inverse makes $u$ invertible by the finite geometric-series inverse for $1+v$ with $v$ nilpotent. Thus $\mathcal O_{A\times T}\xrightarrow{s}\mathcal P_T$ is an isomorphism. Restricting $s$ to the identity section of $A$ gives a unit in $R/I$; divide by it to respect the fixed rigidification. Now [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] identifies $j:T\to B$ with the constant identity map, since their rigidified families are isomorphic. On local rings, the quotient $R\to R/I$ must consequently factor through $R/\mathfrak m=k$. Hence $\mathfrak m\subseteq I$, and together with $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ this proves $I=\mathfrak m$. In particular the dual complex $D$ resolves the reduced residue field, rather than a thickening.

source.place: III §13 p.128, evaluation and the maximal triviality subscheme; the normalized universal property identifies that subscheme with the reduced identity.

proof.text:
Choose $g$ generators $x_1,\ldots,x_g$ of $\mathfrak m$. They form a regular sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], hence a Koszul-regular sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular]. Its Koszul complex resolves $k$. Reindex $D$ as the nonnegative chain resolution with degree $n$ equal to $D^{-n}$. By [lem-sfb-projective-resolution-homotopy-equivalence] it is homotopy equivalent to the augmented Koszul resolution. Dualizing these chain maps and homotopies gives a homotopy equivalence between their dual cochain complexes; finite free double duality (with the standard cochain evaluation signs) identifies the dual of $D$ with $K$. By [lem-sc-koszul-regular-sequence-dual-complex], therefore,
$$K\simeq\bigwedge_k^g\operatorname{Hom}_k(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2,k)[-g].$$
The chosen parameters give a basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, so the displayed determinant is a one-dimensional $k$-space; choosing a nonzero basis identifies it with $k$. Thus $K\simeq k[-g]$ in $D(R)$. When $g=0$, the parameter list is empty, $R=k$ and the determinant is $k$ in degree zero, so the same argument applies.

source.place: III §13 Corollary 1, p.129, comparison with the Koszul resolution; Stacks 0BQZ (duality-lemma-regular-immersion-ext).

proof.text:
By step 2 every cohomology sheaf of $C$ is supported at $e$. The local computation in step 8 gives $\mathcal H^i(C)_e=0$ for $i\ne g$ and $\mathcal H^g(C)_e\cong k$ as $R$-modules, with scalar action through $R\to k$. Hence $\mathcal H^i(C)=0$ for $i\ne g$. Apply [lem-trf-coherent-finite-support-skyscrapers] to $\mathcal H^g(C)$: its singleton support and stalk identify it with the module skyscraper $e_*k$, with precisely the evaluation action in the statement. Finally [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] yields
$$Rp_{2*}\mathcal P_A=C\simeq\mathcal H^g(C)[-g]\simeq e_*k[-g].$$
The only arbitrary choice is a basis of the one-dimensional determinant; the item asserts existence of an isomorphism, not a canonical scalar normalization. All inputs hold in arbitrary characteristic.
